mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 engine replacement typically costs £5,500-£6,600 for a rebuilt unit with supply and fit through a specialist. Used engines start from around £2,500, while main dealer replacement can exceed £12,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling or clicking noise from the front of the engine on cold start. As the problem worsens, you may notice rough idling, hesitation, or a check engine light.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if the chassis and body are in good condition, a rebuilt AJ133 with upgraded components adds significant value and extends the vehicle's life by 100,000+ miles. Given the vehicle's value (£10,000-£25,000+ for a good example), replacement cost is typically well below the car's worth.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 engine replacement typically takes 3-7 days total. This includes 1-2 days for removal and fitting, plus additional time if the replacement engine requires preparation.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 and the SVR engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both use the AJ133 5.0-litre supercharged V8, but the SVR receives a higher state of tune. Standard 5.0 SCV8 produces 510hp and 625Nm, while the SVR produces 550-575hp and 680-700Nm.

mainEntity.name: What causes oil consumption in the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oil consumption on the AJ133 is typically caused by worn valve stem seals or piston ring wear. Consumption of up to 1L per 1,000 miles is common but should be monitored. Severe consumption may indicate bore scoring or ring failure requiring a full rebuild.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 (Supercharged V8) arrived as the performance flagship of the Range Rover Sport line, powered by Jaguar Land Rover's AJ133 5.0-litre supercharged V8 - a direct-injection, all-aluminium 90-degree V8 engine developed at JLR's Bridgend Engine Plant. Over its production life spanning two generations, the engine received multiple power upgrades, culminating in the 575hp SVR variant.

milestones.description: AJ133 5.0-litre supercharged V8 introduced in the L320 generation Range Rover Sport, producing 510hp (375kW) and 625Nm
L494 generation launched; 5.0 SCV8 carries over with 510hp, offered in HSE Dynamic and Autobiography trims
SVR variant debuts with uprated 550hp (405kW) version of the AJ133; torque rises to 680Nm
Post-facelift SVR receives power bump to 567hp (423kW) and 700Nm
SVR engine further revised with ported supercharger, ECU updates, and lightened exhaust system
L461 third-generation launched; 5.0 SCV8 replaced by BMW-sourced 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 (P530)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 5.0L Supercharged V8 Petrol (2009-2022)
items.commonFailure: Timing chain tensioner failure is the most documented issue on the AJ133 5.0 SCV8. The plastic timing chain guides wear prematurely - a problem exacerbated by the factory-recommended 10,000-mile oil service interval, which is considered inadequate for a high-output V8. With excessive chain slack, the timing can jump, causing catastrophic internal engine damage. Cold-start rattle is the primary early warning sign. Typically manifests between 60,000-80,000 miles. Oil consumption (up to 1L per 1,000 miles) is also commonly reported.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 (AJ133) is a high-performance engine with well-documented failure points. Timing chain tensioner failure dominates replacement demand, followed by oil consumption issues and cooling system failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 AJ133 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Plastic timing chain guides wear against the tensioner pins, creating slack in the chains. The factory-recommended 10,000-mile oil service interval accelerates wear on a hot, high-output V8. Cold-start rattle is the first warning sign. If left unaddressed, the chain can jump timing or break, causing catastrophic internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing chains, tensioners, guides, and cam sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early (rattle present, no engine damage). Adds 40,000+ miles of life

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt AJ133 with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chains have failed or engine has suffered collateral damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 of relevant age (2010-2017) is worth approximately £10,000-£25,000 depending on mileage, condition, and specification [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE; Parkers]. SVR models command higher values, with used examples starting from around £26,000. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If you catch timing chain rattle early, the preventative chain replacement is significantly more cost-effective than a full engine swap - specialist pricing from £2,200 makes this a worthwhile investment. However, if the engine has already jumped timing or suffered a snapped chain, a full rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the only reliable path forward. Don't cut corners - the AJ133 is an interference engine; valvetrain damage is almost guaranteed once timing is lost.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failures - Water Pump and Plastic Pipe Deterioration
problems.affectedModels: Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8 (AJ133, all years)
problems.rootCause: The cooling system on the AJ133 has multiple weak points, including the water pump, thermostat, and numerous plastic coolant pipes located under the intake manifold. These plastic components have a limited service life and can become brittle with age and heat cycling. Cooling system failure can lead to overheating and, if ignored, complete engine seizure.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before overheating occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, plastic coolant pipes under intake manifold
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended as preventative maintenance at 70k miles - the plastic pipes have a known service life

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt AJ133 with new cooling components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if overheating has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: Cooling system maintenance is one of the most cost-effective preventative measures on the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SCV8. Replacing the water pump, thermostat, and plastic pipes during timing chain work costs minimal additional labour and can prevent catastrophic failure. If you're already having timing chain work done, it's wise to address the cooling system at the same time.
